egress.terms: Not stated as a number on the listing or the pricing FAQ — "unlimited" is implied by the absence of a meter. **Unverified: I did not find a written egress policy.**

interface_detail: Apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS plus a web browser app; CLI and WebDAV are sold separately and not included.
tooling: The lifetime plan does not include CLI, WebDAV, Backups, Mail, Meet, Cleaner, Password-Protected File Sharing, Advanced Sharing, AI, File versioning or Antivirus, which are sold separately; the listing names no programmatic interface.
chaining: None available on the lifetime SKU without buying the add-ons separately, at which point the price advantage evaporates.
limits_note: "This is available to new users ONLY" and "Codes are NOT stackable" — note this contradicts Internxt's own FAQ ("Internxt lifetime plans are stackable ... up to 100 TB"). Filen-style quota withholding behind VPN IPs is a known Internxt behaviour.

identity_cost.detail: A free Internxt account needs a name and an email address; no identity or email verification is required.

reliability_note: Open-source clients, Securitum-audited, GDPR, fragmentation across servers — technically credible. But the company has run near-continuous 85-91%-off 'lifetime' promotions for years, which is a solvency signal rather than a discount signal, and the StackSocial vs own-site price gap (5 TB $229.99 vs €585) is large enough to make unit economics doubtful.
